text: Top leader calls for expanded sci-tech cooperation with China's Greater Bay Area

HÀ NỘI - Party General Secretary and President Tô Lâm on Tuesday called on Việt Nam and the Greater Bay Area to jointly develop their research, innovation capabilities and master strategically important technologies.

He was speaking at the Việt Nam-China's Greater Bay Area Forum on Technology Connectivity and Innovation held in Shenzhen, which attracted nearly 500 representatives from management agencies, research institutes, universities and businesses in the two countries.

Lâm said Việt Nam and the Greater Bay Area should select fields where their strengths complement each other and where there is practical demand to conduct joint research, starting with AI, semiconductors, robotics and autonomous systems.
According to the top leader, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area brings together research capabilities, manufacturing industries, financial resources and international connectivity.

Shenzhen's development demonstrated the importance of linking innovative thinking and institutional reform with efforts to unleash the creativity of individuals and businesses, he said, adding that these experiences also offered valuable lessons for Việt Nam's development process.

The top Vietnamese leader expressed his hope that cooperation between Việt Nam and the Greater Bay Area in science, technology and workforce training would become a highlight of bilateral relations, with its value reflected in business productivity, people's innovative capacity and quality of life.

He emphasised that training skilled workers and developing talent should be placed at the centre of cooperation, noting that people determine a country's ability to absorb, master and develop technology.
Investment in personnel should thus be regarded as a long-term commitment by partners.

"Việt Nam wishes to strengthen cooperation with training institutions, research institutes and businesses in the Greater Bay Area to develop a workforce of engineers, experts and scientists capable of conducting independent research and addressing complex real-world challenges," Lâm said.

"I propose expanding joint training programmes, co-supervision of doctoral candidates and exchanges of lecturers and experts, while linking academic learning with participation in research projects and practical training at businesses.
"Learners should be given more opportunities to access laboratories, technological processes and modern working environments.

Businesses should participate in identifying training needs, jointly developing curricula and utilising training outcomes, while universities and research institutes ensure a solid knowledge foundation and academic quality.

The top leader said he hoped that young scientists, students and engineers from both countries would have more opportunities to conduct joint research, launch start-ups and contribute to the community.
Lâm called for closer links between innovation and industrial cooperation, with businesses playing a leading role.

Companies should be involved from the outset in identifying research challenges, participate throughout the technology development process and help bring research results into production and business operations, he said.

Việt Nam would welcome long-term investment by corporations and businesses from the Greater Bay Area in establishing research facilities and high-tech manufacturing operations in the country, while strengthening cooperation with domestic enterprises to improve technical capabilities, management and product quality.
He also called on partners to create more opportunities for Vietnamese technology companies to participate in the Greater Bay Area's innovation ecosystem, provide solutions and expand their markets.

The combination of Guangdong's industrial capabilities, Hong Kong's financial strengths and international connectivity and Macao's educational, research and service resources would open up greater opportunities for Vietnamese partners, the leader said.

Noting that Việt Nam will host APEC for the third time in 2027, Lâm expressed the wish to work with APEC member economies to promote new growth drivers, enhance connectivity and expand development opportunities through science, technology and innovation.

He pledged that Việt Nam would stand ready to work alongside partners in the Greater Bay Area with a strong commitment to reform, a spirit of sincere cooperation and responsibility for implementing agreed initiatives.
At the forum, 16 memoranda of understanding between agencies, universities, research organisations and businesses from the two countries were announced and presented.

The agreements cover strategic technology and key industrial sectors, including AI, semiconductors, telecommunications, workforce training, 5G-Advanced, chip design, digital infrastructure, smart cities, urban railways, logistics, digital finance, energy, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and aviation. - VNS
